concepts.name: Definition and Measurement of Noise Pollution: Decibel Scale and Key Parameters
key_dimensions: Distinction between sound, noise, and noise pollution; threshold of hearing vs. threshold of pain
Decibel (dB) scale as a logarithmic (not linear) measure — UPSC trap on proportionality
Key parameters: frequency (Hz), intensity (dB), duration, and time of exposure
Difference between dB and dB(A) — A-weighted scale used in Indian standards

concepts.name: Noise Pollution (Regulation and Control) Rules, 2000: Standards and Zones
key_dimensions: Four ambient noise standard zones: Industrial (75/70 dB), Commercial (65/55 dB), Residential (55/45 dB), Silence (50/40 dB) — day/night distinction
Definition of 'silence zone' — 100-metre radius around hospitals, educational institutions, courts, religious places
Night-time restriction window: 10 PM to 6 AM — applicability and exceptions
2010 and 2017 amendments — loudspeaker restrictions, generator set norms, and firecrackers

concepts.name: Sources and Classification of Noise Pollution
key_dimensions: Transportation noise (road, rail, aviation) vs. industrial noise vs. construction noise vs. neighbourhood noise
Occupational noise as a distinct category — workplace exposure limits under Factories Act
Emerging sources: urban heat island effect amplifying noise, wind turbine noise, sonar noise in marine environments
Indoor vs. outdoor noise pollution — WHO guidelines distinguish both

concepts.name: Health Impacts of Noise Pollution: Auditory and Non-Auditory Effects
key_dimensions: Noise-Induced Hearing Loss (NIHL) — temporary threshold shift vs. permanent threshold shift
Non-auditory effects: hypertension, cardiovascular disease, sleep disturbance, cognitive impairment in children
WHO findings: road traffic noise second-largest environmental health risk in Western Europe after air pollution
Vulnerable groups: children (learning impairment), elderly, hospital patients — basis for silence zone concept

concepts.name: Firecrackers and Noise Pollution: Judicial and Regulatory Framework
key_dimensions: Supreme Court in Noise Pollution (V), In Re (2005) — landmark ruling on firecrackers, loudspeakers, and fundamental rights
Arjun Gopal v. Union of India (2018) — green crackers vs. conventional firecrackers; permitted decibel limits (125 dB at 4 metres)
Distinction between 'green crackers' (reduced emission) and 'improved crackers' — CSIR/NEERI role
Timing restrictions on firecrackers: 8 PM–10 PM on Diwali; SC ban on online sale — enforcement challenges

concepts.name: Loudspeaker and Public Address System Regulation
key_dimensions: Section 144 CrPC (now BNSS) powers of district magistrate to restrict loudspeakers — State vs. Central jurisdiction overlap
Noise Pollution Rules 2000: written permission requirement; 5 dB(A) above ambient limit for public address systems
Night-time absolute ban on loudspeakers except in closed premises with adequate insulation
Religious freedom (Article 25) vs. Right to peaceful living (Article 21) — constitutional tension in judicial rulings

concepts.name: Aviation Noise Regulation: CPCB, DGCA, and Airport Authority Norms
key_dimensions: Aircraft Act 1934 and Environment Protection Act 1986 — jurisdictional overlap in regulating aircraft noise
ICAO Annex 16 standards — Chapter 14 for newer aircraft; India's compliance obligations
Night flight curfew at airports (e.g., Mumbai, Delhi) — economic vs. environmental trade-off
Land-use planning around airports: noise contour maps, Ldn (Day-Night Average Sound Level) metric

concepts.name: Industrial and Occupational Noise: Regulatory Framework
key_dimensions: Factories Act 1948: permissible exposure limit — 90 dB(A) for 8-hour workday (Indian standard vs. WHO's 85 dB recommendation)
Hierarchy of noise controls: elimination → substitution → engineering controls → administrative controls → PPE
Occupational Safety, Health and Working Conditions Code 2020 — consolidation and changes from Factories Act
NIHL as a compensable occupational disease under Employees' Compensation Act — notification requirement

concepts.name: Marine/Underwater Noise Pollution: Impacts on Aquatic Biodiversity
key_dimensions: Anthropogenic sources: shipping, sonar, seismic surveys, offshore drilling — frequency ranges vs. cetacean communication bands
Impact on cetaceans (whales, dolphins): strandings, communication masking, behavioural changes
India's Coastal Regulation Zone (CRZ) rules and Environmental Impact Assessment for offshore activities — noise as underregulated parameter
International frameworks: UNCLOS obligations, IMO guidelines on underwater noise reduction (2014)

concepts.name: Noise Pollution and Urban Planning: Noise Mapping and Land Use
key_dimensions: Strategic noise mapping as a tool — EU Environmental Noise Directive (END) 2002 as a global benchmark India lacks equivalent of
Buffer zones, acoustic barriers, green belts as urban mitigation measures
National Mission for Clean Ganga (NMCG) and Smart Cities Mission — noise pollution as an underaddressed component
Transit-Oriented Development (TOD) paradox: densification near transport corridors increases noise exposure

concepts.name: Role of CPCB and SPCBs in Noise Pollution Monitoring and Enforcement
key_dimensions: CPCB's National Ambient Noise Monitoring Network (NANMN) — cities covered, real-time data gaps
Division of powers: CPCB sets standards, SPCBs enforce — accountability gap in noise compared to air/water
Environment Protection Act 1986, Section 15: penalties for noise violation — imprisonment up to 5 years, fine up to ₹1 lakh
Challenges: noise is transient (no residue), measurement is time-sensitive, complaint-driven enforcement is reactive

concepts.name: Judicial Pronouncements on Noise Pollution and Fundamental Rights
key_dimensions: Church of God (Full Gospel) in India v. K.K.R. Majestic Colony Welfare Association (2000) — no religion mandates use of loudspeakers; Article 25 does not protect right to use sound amplifiers
Noise Pollution (V), In Re (2005) — Right to silence as part of Article 21; State's positive obligation to protect from noise
Farhad Wadia v. Union of India — Bombay HC on firecrackers and Article 21
UPSC trap: distinction between 'right to use loudspeaker' (not fundamental) vs. 'right to religious practice' (fundamental)

concepts.name: Noise Pollution from Construction Activities: Regulation and Gaps
key_dimensions: Construction and Demolition Waste Management Rules 2016 — noise not explicitly addressed; gap vs. air dust norms
CPCB guidelines on construction noise: site boundary limits, working hour restrictions (not uniformly enforced)
Smart Cities and infrastructure boom creating urban construction noise hotspots — UPSC contemporary angle
Comparison with international practice: UK Control of Pollution Act's 'best practicable means' standard

concepts.name: Noise Pollution from Generators and Domestic Equipment
key_dimensions: Environment (Protection) Amendment Rules 2002: DG sets must have acoustic enclosures; 75 dB(A) at 1 metre limit
Bureau of Indian Standards (BIS) and Bureau of Energy Efficiency (BEE) — noise labelling norms for appliances (overlap with energy regulation)
Urban India's dependence on DG sets during power cuts — enforcement paradox during emergencies
Noise from domestic equipment (mixer, TV, AC) as indoor pollution — unregulated under current framework

concepts.name: WHO Guidelines on Environmental Noise (2018): Key Recommendations and India's Gap
key_dimensions: WHO 2018 recommendations: road traffic noise < 53 dB Lden, night noise < 45 dB Lnight — stricter than Indian standards
India's Noise Pollution Rules 2000 vs. WHO 2018 — specific numerical gap for residential zones (55 dB day vs. WHO's 53 dB)
WHO's shift from 'evidence-based' to 'precautionary principle' in 2018 guidelines — policy implication
UPSC trap: WHO 2018 guidelines are 'recommendations,' not binding — India not legally obligated to adopt them

concepts.name: Noise Pollution's Intersection with Biodiversity: Terrestrial Ecosystems
key_dimensions: Anthropogenic noise alters bird song frequency, foraging behaviour, and predator-prey dynamics
Road noise penetrating protected areas — 'road effect zone' concept; up to 1 km impact radius
Impact on pollinator behaviour: bees, bats affected by noise — indirect effect on food security
Eco-Sensitive Zones (ESZ) around national parks — noise from highways and tourism as a regulatory concern under Wildlife Protection Act

concepts.name: Noise Pollution Control Technologies and Green Infrastructure
key_dimensions: Engineering controls: noise barriers (concrete, earth mounds, transparent acrylic), acoustic enclosures, vibration dampers
Green infrastructure: vegetative barriers — effectiveness of trees in noise attenuation (limited, 3–5 dB per 30 metres) — UPSC trap on overestimation
Electric Vehicles (EVs) as noise reduction strategy — but 'quiet car' paradox: EVs pose pedestrian safety risk at low speeds (AVAS mandate)
Smart road surfaces (porous asphalt, rubberised asphalt) — noise reduction co-benefit with drainage

concepts.name: Noise Pollution in the Context of Environmental Impact Assessment (EIA)
key_dimensions: EIA Notification 2006 — noise as a mandatory parameter for Category A and B projects; baseline noise monitoring requirement
Draft EIA 2020 controversy — dilution of public hearing norms affecting noise grievance redressal
Cumulative noise impact assessment — rarely practiced in India; gap compared to EU practice
Post-construction noise monitoring as a condition of Environmental Clearance (EC) — compliance and enforcement gap

concepts.name: International Conventions and Comparative Frameworks on Noise Pollution
key_dimensions: No dedicated international treaty on noise pollution — contrast with air (CLRTAP) and marine pollution (MARPOL) — UPSC trap
EU Environmental Noise Directive (END) 2002 — strategic noise maps, action plans, quiet areas designation; India lacks equivalent
ICAO and IMO voluntary guidelines — sectoral approach vs. comprehensive legislation
Stockholm Declaration (1972) Principle 6 and Rio Declaration — noise as part of 'pollution' broadly defined; basis for domestic legislation

concepts.name: Noise Pollution and Mental Health: Emerging Evidence and Policy Implications
key_dimensions: WHO's 'Burden of Disease from Environmental Noise' (2011) — disability-adjusted life years (DALYs) lost to noise in Europe
Annoyance, sleep disturbance, and cognitive impairment as measurable outcomes — distinction from direct physiological harm
Night-time noise as more harmful than equivalent daytime noise — basis for stricter night standards in Rules 2000
Urban-rural noise divide — rural sound environments as positive health resource ('restorative environments') — emerging policy concept
